Alice L (arch): thinking out loud — we need a concrete plan for endpoint cert rotation + idle connection teardown for private endpoints. earlier RFC covered peering vs private endpoints but not this interaction.
Ben R (neteng): +1. cert rotation currently forces short-lived TLS renegotiation; if we tear idle conns aggressively we lose warm gRPC pools. tradeoff: security vs latency/cost.
Carla M (sre): observed in canary: customers with long-lived websocket/kafka over endpoint saw 30% errors during rotation window. Need graceful drain.
Ben R (neteng): proposal: stagger rotations per AZ and mark connections draining via HTTP header before cert swap. clients should reconnect with new cert.
Dmitri K (infra): ops constraints: some customers pin IPs and blacklist churn. Staggering increases rotation window — risk if cert compromised. We need a kill-switch to force immediate rotation (and accept reconnections).
Alice L (arch): ok so design options: 1) short TTL certs + global rolling but slower drain; 2) long TTL + heartbeat/keepalive to detect stale conns; 3) maintain proxy in CP that can swap certs transparently.
Carla M (sre): option 3 seems nicest for UX but increases control plane responsibility and private deployment complexity (customer-managed CP can't inject proxy easily). Also makes private plane a target for perf regressions.
Ben R (neteng): technical sketch for option 1 (short TTL + stagger):
```
- rotate certs for subset of endpoints (AZ) at t0
- set endpoint header: x-endpoint-draining: true
- set TCP FIN_WAIT timer to 30s for draining connections
- clients must retry l7 after 3xx/401 and re-TLS
```
Carla M (sre): from incidents: 30s FIN_WAIT caused user-visible tail-latency spikes. We should default to 120s for hosted, but expose config for Dedicated/Private.
Dmitri K (infra): also need DB of connection state for long-lived sessions? Otherwise we can't correlate session ownership during migration. That's a big refactor (session store + sticky routing).
Alice L (arch): SPIKE idea: implement a lightweight connection-metadata cache in control plane for only sessions > 5m. Not full session store. Could reduce refactor scope.
Ben R (neteng): quick checklist for rollout (canary -> prod):
- implement draining header + metrics (drain_start, conn_close_success)
- default idle timeout config per deployment type (hosted:120s, dedicated:300s, private: configurable)
- add deploy-bot policy to allow emergency force-rotate
- doc for customers about retry semantics and IP pinning impacts

erica (deploy-bot): deploy status: rotation-fix branch CI passed, canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-25T16:00Z. :rocket:

Carla M (sre): operational playbook snippet for incident responders:
```
1) run: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE' https://controlplane/api/v1/drain-status?az=us-west-2
2) if drain stuck > 10m: scale up proxy pods: k scale deploy endpoint-proxy --replicas=+2 -n infra
3) to force rotate: POST /controlplane/api/v1/rotate?force=true (auth required)
```

Dmitri K (infra): follow-ups: schedule perf test for 10k long-lived conns across 3 AZs; measure reconnection churn under stagger vs immediate. I'll own the spike.
Alice L (arch): action items: Ben implement draining header + config knobs, Carla add SRE runbook + metrics, Dmitri run perf spike, I'll draft RFC follow-up with decision matrix and emergency rollback semantics.
Ben R (neteng): I can have a PR with draining header and docs by EOD Friday.
Carla M (sre): tagging ops-oncall for visibility @oncall-netops :eyes:
Alice L (arch): thanks all. leaving this thread as the coordination point for the spike and rollout plan.
